- When sentiment is negative and persistent, model tends to underpredict prices; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After sharp price spikes, model often overreacts and overshoots; reduce forecast by 5–10% in the immediate 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently fails to capture the momentum; increase forecast slope by 0.5–1.5% per day.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in early forecast windows; for 30-day horizon, apply a 1–3% downward bias if recent 7-day average is below 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates upward momentum; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast if sentiment > 0.10 over last 5 days.
- Lagged sentiment (e.g., 3–5 day average) should be weighted more heavily than current sentiment for 10+ day forecasts; use sentiment lag as a multiplier for adjustment.
